verdict.rationale: Twenty documents REST and GraphQL APIs with batch create, update and delete of up to 60 records per request, plus GraphQL batch upsert. It also documents outbound webhooks on record create, update and delete, which give change detection for syncing from Twenty to another system. Rate limits are never documented in the evidence, upsert is only stated for GraphQL, and scale guidance is thin beyond 'Unlimited' API import and the 60-record batch cap. Missing for 10: documented API rate limits, REST upsert, cursor- or timestamp-based incremental change queries, explicit guidance for bidirectional sync at scale, independent hands-on corroboration of sync at volume.

support.subject: As a developer, I can sync records bidirectionally through the API at scale, with documented rate limits, upserts, and change detection

citations.quote: Both REST and GraphQL support batching up to 60 records per request — create, update, or delete. GraphQL also supports batch upsert
Twenty sends an HTTP POST to your URL whenever a record is created, updated, or deleted.
Both GraphQL and REST endpoints, with auto-generated documentation per workspace.
